author: NorthEast News Desk
body: United Arab Emirates stock markets closed higher Friday as a sharp weekly rise in oil prices offset continued concern about shipping disruptions in the Middle East. Dubai’s benchmark advanced 0.6% after two losing sessions, while Abu Dhabi’s index edged up 0.03% for a fourth consecutive gain.

Emirates NBD, Dubai’s largest lender, rose 4.2%, and district-cooling company Empower gained 1.9%. In Abu Dhabi, investment firm Two Point Zero added 3.6%, Adnoc Logistics & Services climbed 2.9%, and NMDC Group gained 3.5%. Declines in Fertiglobe and First Abu Dhabi Bank limited the broader index’s advance.

The figures are Friday closing data, not live prices. Crude was on course for a weekly gain of more than 7% as attacks and reduced vessel traffic raised concern about persistent supply constraints. For the full week, Abu Dhabi’s benchmark gained 1.4% and Dubai’s added 1%, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. The moves show investors balancing stronger energy-linked revenue expectations against escalating regional risk.
dek: Dubai’s benchmark rose 0.6% at Friday’s close, while Abu Dhabi edged higher for a fourth session amid pressure on regional shipping routes.
headline: UAE shares finish higher as oil-supply concerns support markets
